name: Learn: kubeadm (upgrade, join, certs, maintenance)
objective: CKA › Cluster Architecture, Installation & Configuration (25%). Drill EVERY node-level kubeadm corner harder than the exam: inspect component versions, read the kubelet config and static-pod manifests, mint a worker join token, perform the drain/uncordon maintenance dance, renew control-plane certificates, read an upgrade plan, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix. All graded exactly on persistent node/cluster state.
description: Eight strict node-level practicals on a kubeadm-managed kind cluster. Reach the node binaries and files with docker exec into $CP/$W1/$W2. Each Check shows which requirements you met and the exact reason for any you missed.

questions.title: Inspect component versions
questions.teach:
Before any upgrade, read what you're running. `kubeadm version -o short` prints the CLI tag; `kubelet --version` prints `Kubernetes v...`. Both binaries live on the node, so reach them with `docker exec` into $CP.

**Gotcha:** a redirect like `docker exec "$CP" kubelet --version > /tmp/f` writes to YOUR host, not the node — redirect INSIDE the node: `docker exec "$CP" sh -c '... > /tmp/f'`.
questions.prompt:
On the control-plane node ($CP), capture the kubeadm and kubelet versions and write BOTH, one per line, to `/tmp/versions.txt` on $CP.

Target: `docker exec "$CP" cat /tmp/versions.txt` shows a `kubeadm`/`v…` line and a `Kubernetes v...` (kubelet) line.
questions.hint: Redirect INSIDE the node: `docker exec "$CP" sh -c 'kubeadm version -o short > /tmp/versions.txt; kubelet --version >> /tmp/versions.txt'`. Confirm with `docker exec "$CP" cat /tmp/versions.txt`.
questions.solution:
docker exec "$CP" sh -c 'kubeadm version -o short > /tmp/versions.txt; kubelet --version >> /tmp/versions.txt'
docker exec "$CP" cat /tmp/versions.txt

verification.description: /tmp/versions.txt on $CP has a kubeadm version line + a kubelet 'Kubernetes v...' line

questions.title: Read the kubelet's config file
questions.teach:
A kubeadm node's kubelet is driven by `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml` (a `KubeletConfiguration`). The `cgroupDriver` there MUST match the container runtime's — a mismatch stops the kubelet from starting. Read the file on the node with `docker exec`.

**Gotcha:** this is the component config, NOT the `kubeadm-config` ConfigMap in kube-system — don't confuse the two.
questions.prompt:
On $CP, read `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml` and write ONLY the value of its `cgroupDriver` field (e.g. `systemd` or `cgroupfs`) to `/tmp/cgroupdriver.txt` on $CP.

Target: `/tmp/cgroupdriver.txt` on $CP contains exactly the cgroupDriver value, nothing else.
questions.hint: Grep the field inside the node and strip the key: `docker exec "$CP" sh -c "grep cgroupDriver /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml | awk '{print \$2}' > /tmp/cgroupdriver.txt"`. Confirm with `docker exec "$CP" cat /tmp/cgroupdriver.txt`.
questions.solution:
docker exec "$CP" sh -c "grep cgroupDriver /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml | awk '{print \$2}' > /tmp/cgroupdriver.txt"
docker exec "$CP" cat /tmp/cgroupdriver.txt

questions.title: Read a static Pod manifest
questions.teach:
The control-plane components run as **static Pods** — the kubelet starts them straight from manifest files in `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/` (no API server needed). `kube-apiserver.yaml` there pins the apiserver's exact image, which is the version an upgrade bumps.

**Gotcha:** editing these files restarts the component immediately — here you only READ, so don't modify them.
questions.prompt:
On $CP, read `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml` and write the apiserver container's full `image:` value (e.g. `registry.k8s.io/kube-apiserver:v1.31.0`) to `/tmp/apiserver-image.txt` on $CP.

Target: `/tmp/apiserver-image.txt` on $CP contains an image reference ending in a `kube-apiserver:v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` tag.
questions.hint: Pull the image line inside the node: `docker exec "$CP" sh -c "grep 'image:' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml | awk '{print \$2}' > /tmp/apiserver-image.txt"`. Confirm with `docker exec "$CP" cat /tmp/apiserver-image.txt`.
questions.solution:
docker exec "$CP" sh -c "grep 'image:' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml | awk '{print \$2}' > /tmp/apiserver-image.txt"
docker exec "$CP" cat /tmp/apiserver-image.txt

verification.description: /tmp/apiserver-image.txt on $CP holds the kube-apiserver image:tag from the static manifest

questions.title: Generate a worker join command
questions.teach:
To add a worker, mint a fresh bootstrap token and print the full join line in one shot: `kubeadm token create --print-join-command`. This creates a Secret named `bootstrap-token-<id>` of type `bootstrap.kubernetes.io/token` in `kube-system`.

**Gotcha:** find these Secrets by TYPE, not name — `kubectl -n kube-system get secrets --field-selector type=bootstrap.kubernetes.io/token`.
questions.prompt:
On $CP, generate a fresh worker join command with kubeadm so a NEW bootstrap-token Secret is created in `kube-system`.

Target: strictly MORE bootstrap-token Secrets exist in `kube-system` than when the step started.
questions.hint: `docker exec "$CP" kubeadm token create --print-join-command`. Verify with `kubectl -n kube-system get secrets --field-selector type=bootstrap.kubernetes.io/token`.
questions.solution:
docker exec "$CP" kubeadm token create --print-join-command
kubectl -n kube-system get secrets --field-selector type=bootstrap.kubernetes.io/token

verification.description: a NEW bootstrap-token Secret was created in kube-system (count increased)

questions.title: Drain then uncordon a node
questions.teach:
For node maintenance you `drain` (cordon + evict pods), do the work, then `uncordon` to let the scheduler use the node again: `kubectl drain <node>`, then `kubectl uncordon <node>`.

**Gotcha:** plain `drain` errors on real nodes — you need `--ignore-daemonsets`, plus `--force` to evict a bare (unmanaged) pod and `--delete-emptydir-data` if a pod uses emptyDir.
questions.prompt:
A bare Pod `drain-me` is pinned to worker $W2. Drain $W2 (evicting the workload), then uncordon it when "maintenance" is done.

Target: $W2 ends `schedulable` (`.spec.unschedulable` unset) AND no running `drain-me` pod remains on $W2.
questions.hint: `kubectl drain "$W2" --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force`, confirm with `kubectl get pods -o wide`, then `kubectl uncordon "$W2"`.
questions.solution:
kubectl drain "$W2" --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
kubectl get pods -o wide
kubectl uncordon "$W2"
kubectl get node "$W2"

verification.description: $W2 is schedulable and holds no running drain-me pod

questions.title: Renew control-plane certificates
questions.teach:
kubeadm control-plane certs under `/etc/kubernetes/pki/` last ONE year. Check them with `kubeadm certs check-expiration`, then renew with `kubeadm certs renew apiserver` (or `renew all`), pushing NotAfter ~1 year out and writing a fresh cert (new serial).

**Gotcha:** renewal rewrites the cert on disk but does NOT restart the static pod — the running apiserver keeps the old cert until its manifest is bounced.
questions.prompt:
On $CP, check cert expiration, then renew the apiserver certificate so a fresh cert (new serial, NotAfter ~1 year out) is written.

Target: `/etc/kubernetes/pki/apiserver.crt` on $CP has a DIFFERENT serial than when the step started, and its NotAfter is >300 days out.
questions.hint: `docker exec "$CP" kubeadm certs check-expiration`, then `docker exec "$CP" kubeadm certs renew apiserver`. Confirm: `docker exec "$CP" openssl x509 -enddate -serial -noout -in /etc/kubernetes/pki/apiserver.crt`.
questions.solution:
docker exec "$CP" kubeadm certs check-expiration
docker exec "$CP" kubeadm certs renew apiserver
docker exec "$CP" openssl x509 -enddate -serial -noout -in /etc/kubernetes/pki/apiserver.crt

verification.description: apiserver.crt serial changed AND NotAfter is >300 days out (renewed)

questions.title: Read a kubeadm upgrade plan
questions.teach:
`kubeadm upgrade plan` is a READ-ONLY report: it lists which versions you can upgrade to and the components it would bump. You run it before `kubeadm upgrade apply v1.X.Y`. The plan reasons about the running server (apiserver) version, which `kubectl version` reports.

**Gotcha:** parse the version with `kubectl version -o json` — the old `--short` flag was removed.
questions.prompt:
On $CP, run `kubeadm upgrade plan` to read it. To prove the control plane is healthy and reporting a version, write the server (apiserver) version string to `/tmp/serverversion.txt` on $CP.

Target: `/tmp/serverversion.txt` on $CP contains a `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` Kubernetes version.
questions.hint: `docker exec "$CP" kubeadm upgrade plan`. Then capture the server version onto the node: `docker exec "$CP" sh -c 'kubectl --kubeconfig /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf version -o json | grep -oE "v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+" | head -1 > /tmp/serverversion.txt'`.
questions.solution:
docker exec "$CP" kubeadm upgrade plan
docker exec "$CP" sh -c 'kubectl --kubeconfig /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf version -o json | grep -oE "v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+" | head -1 > /tmp/serverversion.txt'
docker exec "$CP" cat /tmp/serverversion.txt

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a Pod that won't schedule
questions.teach:
A Pod stuck `Pending` with no node is a scheduling problem. `kubectl describe pod

` Events show the reason — a common one is every candidate node being `unschedulable` (cordoned), so the scheduler has nowhere to place it. **Gotcha:** fix the NODE (uncordon it), not the pod — an already-created Pending pod schedules on its own once a matching node becomes schedulable.
questions.prompt:
Pod `maint-app` in `default` is stuck `Pending` — it is pinned (via nodeSelector) to a worker that is currently cordoned. Diagnose WHY it won't schedule and fix it so it runs. Do NOT delete or recreate the pod, and do NOT edit the pod's nodeSelector.

Target: pod `maint-app` is `Running` AND the worker it targets is schedulable.
questions.hint: `kubectl describe pod maint-app` and `kubectl get nodes` — one worker shows `SchedulingDisabled`. That's $W1. Uncordon it: `kubectl uncordon "$W1"`, then watch `kubectl get pod maint-app -o wide`.
questions.solution:
kubectl describe pod maint-app
kubectl get nodes
# $W1 is cordoned (SchedulingDisabled) and maint-app's nodeSelector pins it there
kubectl uncordon "$W1"
kubectl get pod maint-app -o wide

verification.description: maint-app is Running and its target worker ($W1) is schedulable
